Definition: One fact about an item, such as its name, position or mass, that can be read and changed.
Rules that make items move like real objects: falling, sliding, bouncing and pushing each other.
A push or a pull. Forces are measured in newtons, named after Isaac Newton. One newton is about the force it takes to hold up a small apple.
How much matter an item has, measured in kilograms. Heavier items are harder to push.
The pull that makes things fall. On Earth, it speeds a falling thing up by about 9.8 meters per second, every second.
How much an item resists sliding against something else.
Whether physics can move an item, and whether forces like gravity act on it.
The small slice of time physics moves forward each time it runs. In Quorum it is 1/60 of a second.
